:::{#sol-epe-three-sources}

1. The expected squared error is the sum of the three sources:
   $1 + 2 + 3 = 6$.

2. $0 + 0 + 3 = 3$.
   The noise variance $\varpar = 3$ remains,
   so $3$ is the smallest expected squared error any prediction can have here.

3. A better method can reduce the squared bias and the variance of $\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}$,
   because both depend on how $\fitproc$ is built.
   It cannot reduce $\varpar$,
   which is the variance of the noise $\noise$ in the new outcome.

:::
